Nonparametric regression via TDNN rank weights

Source: R/user-tdnn-npr.R
np_tdnn.Rd

Estimate a localized nonparametric mean by combining observed outcomes with Demirkaya two-scale DNN (TDNN) local weights. TDNN is a signed linear combination of two DNN tables at orders s1 < s2; the combination cancels the leading bias term and achieves a faster MSE rate than single-scale DNN under sufficient smoothness.

Usage

np_tdnn(
  data = NULL,
  x_cols = NULL,
  y_col = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  X = NULL,
  Y = NULL,
  X0 = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  distance = "l2",
  method = c("exact", "asymp"),
  s1 = 1L,
  s2 = 2L,
  dim = NULL,
  normalize = TRUE,
  se = TRUE,
  jackknife = c("fast", "loo", "none"),
  ctx = NULL,
  return = c("W")
)

Arguments

data

Optional data frame (or tibble) containing covariates and the outcome column. Column names must be non-missing, non-empty, and unique.

x_cols

Names or integer indices of covariate columns in data.

y_col

Name or integer index of the outcome column in data.

y

Optional numeric outcome vector of length n. In the data-frame interface, use this instead of y_col.

X

Numeric matrix (n x p) for the matrix interface.

Y

Numeric outcome vector of length n for the matrix interface.

X0

Numeric matrix (m x p) of target points; mutually exclusive with x0.

x0

Numeric vector of length p for a single target point.

distance

Distance name or specification (for example "l2").

method

One of "exact" or "asymp" for TDNN rank weights.

s1

Positive integer; smaller U-statistic order. Must satisfy s1 < s2.

s2

Positive integer; larger U-statistic order. Must satisfy s1 < s2 <= n.

dim

Positive integer; localization dimension. Defaults to ncol(X) when NULL.

normalize

Logical; renormalize the asymptotic rank table to sum 1 (only used when method = "asymp"; default TRUE).

se

Logical; compute delete-1 jackknife standard errors.

jackknife

One of "fast", "loo", or "none". "fast" (default) uses the prefix/suffix rank-order engine; "loo" recomputes leave-one-out weights from scratch; "none" skips SEs entirely.

ctx

Optional context passed through to distance and rank-weight evaluators.

return

Optional extras in addition to the always-returned mu, se, and meta. Allowed values: c("W", "ranks", "ord", "dx", "y", "ess", "neighbors"). The neighbors extra returns the nearest observation for each target; it is not the TDNN signed weight support.

Value

An object of class tdnn_np_result with components:

  • mu: estimated local mean values at target points;

  • se: optional jackknife standard errors;

  • x0: the m x p matrix of evaluation points, with covariate column names propagated from the training data when available;

  • meta: metadata (n, m, p, s1, s2, dim, method, distance);

  • optional extras requested via return.

Details

Two interfaces are supported.

  1. Data-frame interface (recommended): pass data, x_cols, and exactly one of y_col or y.

  2. Matrix interface: pass X, one of X0 or x0, and Y.

Signed weights. The columns of the TDNN weight matrix sum to 1, but individual entries can be negative. This is expected and reflects the bias-correction structure; it does not indicate numerical problems.

Localization dimension. dim governs the rate at which TDNN order weights decay with rank. It defaults to ncol(X) (the covariate dimension) and should be overridden only when a custom distance has a different effective dimension.

Jackknife. "fast" (default) uses the prefix/suffix rank-order engine (jackknife_rank_full()), which precomputes the TDNN rank tables at n and n-1 once and runs an \(O(n \cdot m)\) loop without re-evaluating the distance. "loo" recomputes weights from scratch for each deletion and is useful for validation.

See also

weights_tdnn(), np_dnn(), np_demo_data().

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 80
x_mat <- matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n, 2)
y_vec <- x_mat[, 1] - 0.5 * x_mat[, 2] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)
out <- np_tdnn(
  X = x_mat, x0 = c(0, 0), Y = y_vec,
  distance = "l2", method = "exact", s1 = 2L, s2 = 4L,
  se = FALSE, return = c("W", "ess")
)
out$mu
#> [1] 0.04952335
